"vyos-qemu" above is the full VyOS QEMU image from labhub (VERIFIED 2026-06-01).
2026-08-08 (REAL BUG, found by 83-device-matrix's "VyOS - real Power on click reaches
running state"): this said `vyos/vyos:latest`, a reference that DOES NOT EXIST. The
`vyos/vyos` Docker Hub repository is not published at all - verified live, both
`docker manifest inspect vyos/vyos:latest` and `:1.4-rolling` return "no such manifest",
and node-manager logs the pull as
docker.errors.NotFound: failed to resolve reference "docker.io/vyos/vyos:latest": not found
so the built-in VyOS palette device could never boot for ANY user, on any install.
The platform already ships the working community image everywhere else it matters -
docker_provider.py's _CONTAINER_NOS_LAUNCH has a live-verified privileged/tmpfs profile
keyed on "ghcr.io/sysoleg/vyos-container" (2026-07-25), models.py lists it in
PRIVILEGED_VENDOR_IMAGE_PREFIXES, and VendorIcon maps 'vyos-container' -> vyos - only
this catalog entry (and its frontend/taxonomy mirrors) still pointed at the dead one.

reasons.boot_timeout_sec:
boot_timeout_sec bumped 10 -> 180 (NPX-567, 2026-08-26, live-timed): the
image's own first-boot default-config commit (what creates the "vyos" login
user docker_provider.py's new readiness_cmds now gates on) took 89s/83s across
two clean throwaway-container runs. 10s left no margin at all - every apply
against this profile raced a container that could not yet be considered
RUNNING. 180s matches the margin convention used for the other docker NOS
profiles here (srlinux 120s for a comparably heavy app-manager boot).
